Constructors under the cross-language names

Source: R/ast-constructors.R
multimod-constructors.Rd

Aliases for the AST and model constructors, spelled the way the same type is spelled in C++ and Python (Set("tech") rather than new_set("tech")). They call the existing constructors and return the same objects; the original names are unaffected.

Usage

Set(...)

Mapping(...)

Parameter(...)

Variable(...)

Equation(...)

SetRef(...)

MappingRef(...)

ParameterRef(...)

VariableRef(...)

Symbol(...)

Dims(...)

Constant(...)

Expression(...)

Unary(...)

When(...)

Func(...)

Sum(...)

Prod(...)

SetMin(...)

SetMax(...)

Shift(...)

Call(...)

Where(...)

Arguments

...

Arguments passed to the underlying constructor.

Value

An AST node.

Details

Declarations take the bare name (Set(), Parameter(), Variable(), Mapping(), Equation()); references take a Ref suffix (SetRef(), ParameterRef(), VariableRef(), MappingRef()). The two are structurally different objects - see ast_schema().

See also

ast_schema(), new_set(), ast_set()

Examples

Set("tech")                      # a declaration
#> <AST set> tech
SetRef("tech")                   # a reference
#> <AST set> tech
Expression("*", Symbol("a"), Symbol("b"))
#> <AST expression> *
#>   lhs :
#> <AST symbol> a
#>   rhs:
#> <AST symbol> b
